scope: The surviving Stadium of Delphi as photographed in March 2012, including the open track, north limestone tiers, curved west end, southern terrace remnants and east starting-line and entrance remains.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The archaeological site record describes twelve surviving north rows, six rows at the west curve, the south terrace collapse, east entrance supports and starting stones, and historical course dimensions.
UNESCO describes the stadium’s role in the Pythian Games and location in the Delphi archaeological site.

sectionBasis: Open excavation with twelve surviving north seat rows, six curved west rows, rear stone wall, eroded southern terrace and low eastern starting stones and entrance remains.
